actionable_steps.step: Go about your daily work and duties, but keep your mind resting on God through it all.

actionable_steps.citation: Triple transformation : Sankraanthi's call — SSS Vol 29 (1996), 1996-01-15
actionable_steps.step: Turn the intellect inward toward the heart for a few quiet minutes each day; the bliss experienced within alone is true bliss.

actionable_steps.citation: Neither Scriptures Nor Logic — SSS Vol 1 (1953 - 60), 1959-04-12
actionable_steps.step: Develop bliss by cultivating love — begin in your own home and let it spread to every creature.
Serve others in a spirit of humility, without condescension; service steadies the mind for Atmic experience.

definition.citation: Bliss Is Your Real Form — SSS Vol 29 (1996), 1996-08-01
definition.quote: When sugar and water are separate, sugar is sugar and water is water. When they combine, you get syrup. Similarly, when sat and chit come together, bliss is the result. Bliss is your real form.

discourses.citation: Dwell in God Consciousness — SSS Vol 32 (1999), 1999-04-27
discourses.quote: Bliss is with you. Bliss is in you. It is behind you, above you, below you and all around you. When you are immersed in bliss, what is it that you need to search?

discourses.citation: Light the lamp within — SSS Vol 24 (1991), 1991-11-05
discourses.quote: There is a wide gulf between "Bliss" and "pleasure." The latter is temporary... He must aspire for the Ananda that is everlasting.

discourses.citation: Vital role of the Buddhi — SSS Vol 30 (1997), 1997-10-08
discourses.quote: The source of bliss is within man, not in the external world. God is omnipresent and is not separate from you.

After a term of deep sleep, man declares that he had unbroken Ananda. The mind and the senses, even the faculty of reason, had no contact then with any object, nor did they have any impact from objects. So, the Ananda was derived, during sleep, from within his own reality.

make_it_real: Bliss is not something to chase — it is what you are. Stop hunting for it outside and turn inward.
title: Bliss (Ananda)

vahinis.quote: From all outside you, grief; From all within you, happiness... when one feels that one's spiritual bliss (ananda) is dependent on external objects, one is moving beyond oneself and courting grief. One plunges into needless grief by the enslavement to objects that, according to one's fancy, can make one happy.
